data.hypothesis: With the fixed 128-thread CTA, each warp can reduce its lanes using the existing helper, while the final warp needs only shuffle-down offsets 2 and 1 to combine its four warp totals. This targeted final combine may reduce CTA-local work versus a general 32-lane reduction, but the measured candidates suggest that any local change may be masked by complete-run costs. The launch geometry, one-value-per-lane loading, stage schedule, scratch selection, and final copy stay fixed so the controller can test the local change independently of topology.

memory_lessons.applicability: The reduction schedule and launch topology are held fixed here, so prior complete-run comparisons are relevant but do not isolate which CTA-local instructions caused the timing differences.
memory_lessons.claim: The supplied valid candidates measured 29.215 μs for default CUB BlockReduce, 29.729 μs for explicit CUB warp reductions, and 30.066 μs for a warp-centric reduction. These measurements favor default CUB among those runs but do not establish the cause or predict this candidate.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Compare this candidate's repeated complete-run timings and correctness against the measured CUB and warp-centric candidates.

data.notes: This candidate retains the supplied base program's 128-thread launches, multi-stage scratch schedule, and final copy. Tail lanes contribute zero, and all lanes in the warp-level reductions participate. The prior three candidates passed all 10 supplied correctness cases; their reported means range from 29.215 μs to 30.066 μs. No performance or correctness result is claimed for this proposal; the controller must validate and measure it.
transformations: Replace reduce0's modulo-based shared-memory tree with one warp-local reduction per warp, followed by a single CTA barrier.
Use the existing warpReduceSum helper for lane reductions, then combine the four warp totals using only shuffle-down offsets 2 and 1 in warp 0.
Load one value per lane and use zero for out-of-range tail lanes; preserve the 128-thread launch, multi-stage scratch schedule, scratch selection, and final copy.
